title: Ontology of Belief Diversity: A Community-Based Epistemological Approach
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured belief fairness in a large language model by prompting it with questions about various belief systems and then applying sentiment analysis to the generated text. The goal was to see if the sentiment of the model's responses was consistent and fair across different beliefs.
findings: The paper found that its proposed epistemological ontology (grouping beliefs by Perception, Introspection, and Testimony) can help with fairness testing for all religions without direct enumeration. Sentiment analysis on a large language model's outputs revealed that beliefs within a mid-level category (e.g., testimony-related religions) had correlated sentiment scores. This suggests that fairness testing on their identified subset of beliefs may generalize to a much larger pool of belief systems. The study also noted that Agnosticism and Atheism tended to receive the lowest sentiment scores in generated responses.
